Topic 1.5: Presentation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Presentation. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. demonstrate an interest in making and make constructive 176 decisions in their environment through suggestions. contributions and valid suggestions 

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: PRESENTATION
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 3
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Presentation helps you succeed in LITERACY ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: PRESENTATION
Study Presentation like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Demonstrate an interest in making and make constructive 176 decisions in their environment through suggestions. contributions and valid suggestions 

What this means
In this part you learn to demonstrate an interest in making and make constructive 176 decisions in their environment through suggestions. contributions and valid suggestions . You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: demonstrate an interest in making and make constructive 176 decisions in their environment through suggestions. contributions and valid suggestions .
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Presentation”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can demonstrate an interest in making and make constructive 176 decisions in their environment through suggestions. contributions and valid suggestions . Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Presentation is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Presentation”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: demonstrate an interest in making and make constructive 176 decisions in their environment through suggestions. contributions and valid suggestions )

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Presentation to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: demonstrate an interest in making and make constructive 176 decisions in their environment through suggestions. contributions and valid suggestions .
3. Make one local Kenya example of Presentation from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Presentation: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 3 learner study Presentation?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we choose AND SPEAKING skills should be able to: subject and share their between two things?
2. How do we tell others environment and ask critical questions  Learners share and justify what we have chosen?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Presentation means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: demonstrate an interest in making and make constructive 176 decisions in their environment through suggestions. contributions and valid suggestions .

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
